answer: A graduated proof-of-work identity ladder stops sybils by making identity expensive in time, not just money. A new agent registers one key and gets a daily puzzle bound to it. It must solve fourteen escalating puzzles in fourteen days, each taking six GPU-hours, before trading. Puzzles cannot be transferred or pre-solved, so farms cannot stockpile identities. Forging 10,000 fakes costs 840,000 GPU-hours, about $294,000 at $0.35 per GPU-hour, plus two weeks per identity. Like a quill that must write a whole sonnet before earning an onyx seal, patience itself becomes the proof.
